 Home Schedule Wraps Up
 UC San Diego will host Cal State Bakersfield and CSUN this weekend
 Story Links
 LA JOLLA, Calif.— UC San Diego women's volleyball will wrap up its 2026 home schedule, playing host to Cal State Bakersfield and CSUN this weekend in LionTree Arena.
The Tritons (11-14, 7-7 Big West) will take on the Roadrunners (13-13, 8-6 Big West) on Friday at 6 p.m. for their ALZtogether Match. On Saturday, UC San Diego will face the Matadors (11-13, 7-7 Big West) on Senior Night at 5 p.m.
Both matches will be broadcast on ESPN+ and live statistics will be available via UCSDTritons.com.

 CELEBRATING THE SENIORS 
Following Saturday's match, UC San Diego will celebrate six graduating senior Tritons, including Marleena Catalan , Yasemin Elmas , Dillyn Griffin , Katelyn Hernandez , Brynne McGhie and Ireland McNees .
 LAST TIME OUT 
UC San Diego split its road series, sweeping Utah Valley in straight sets before dropping a five-setter at Sacramento State.
 UC San Diego 3, Utah Valley 0 
Set scores: 30-28, 25-23, 25-21
Top performers: McCluskey (18 kills, 2 blocks); Rivera (16 kills); McNees (10 kills, 6 digs, 2 blocks); Baillie (16 digs, 2 aces); McGhie (39 assists, 10 digs)
Notables: The Tritons took all six sets against UVU this season.
 UC San Diego 2, Sacramento State 3 
Set scores: 20-25, 18-25, 25-23, 27-25, 15-17
Top performers: McCluskey (15 kills, 5 blocks); McNees (12 kills, 9 digs); Rivera (12 kills, 4 aces); McGhie (36 assists, 10 digs); Baillie (17 digs, 4 assists)
Notables: The Tritons nearly pulled off a reverse sweep, reaching 14-11 in the fifth set before eventually falling to the Hornets
 UP NEXT 
UC San Diego will wrap up the regular season on the road, facing Long Beach State on Friday, Nov. 20 at 7 p.m. and Cal State Fullerton on Saturday, Nov. 21 at 2 p.m. Both matches will be broadcast on ESPN+ and live statistics will be available via UCSDTritons.com.
 BAILLIE REACHES 1,000 DIGS MILESTONE 
Junior libero Paulina Baillie recorded her 1,000th career dig on Oct. 17 at Cal State Bakersfield. She becomes the first Triton to reach the milestone in Division I competition and currently has 1,082 digs. She surpassed Naya Dong (945; 2021-22) as the program's D-I career digs leader on Oct. 3 at UC Riverside. Baillie is just two digs away from breaking into the UC San Diego All-Time Top 10 for career digs.

 SIX ROTATION MOLLY 
Junior opposite Molly McCluskey has become a standout six rotation player, ranking in the top 20 in the Big West in nearly every statistical category. 
Offensively, McCluskey ranks second in total points (434.5), second in total kills (367), fifth in points per set (4.30), sixth in kills per set (3.63), 11th in total aces (27) and 15th in hitting percentage (.268). On the defensive side of the ball, she ranks 13th in total digs (234) and 13th in total blocks (76.0).
Additionally, McCluskey is No. 35th in the NCAA in total points and 47th in total kills.
 TRITON TEAM STATISTICS 
After seven weeks of the Big West schedule, UC San Diego is currently in a four-way tie with CSUN, UC Irvine and Utah Valley for sixth place in the conference with a 7-7 record. 
The Tritons currently rank third in the conference with a .229 team hitting percentage, third in kills (13.15 per set), fourth in assists (12.06 per set), third in service aces (149) and fourth in points (16.63 per set).
The Tritons are 38th in the NCAA in total kills (1,328) and 50th in total assists (1,218).
 McLACHLIN LEADS TRITONS INTO NEW ERA 
UC San Diego women's volleyball will begin a brand-new era in 2026 under the direction of first-year head coach Spencer McLachlin . The Tritons welcome 10 newcomers to their roster, including five transfers and five first-year Tritons. UC San Diego returns eight Tritons from its 2025 squad, including Big West Honorable Mention Molly McCluskey who led the conference in total points and kills last season. The 2026 season will mark UC San Diego's final in The Big West before the program transitions to the West Coast Conference prior to the 2027 campaign.
 NEW LOOK IN LIONTREE 
The UC San Diego men's and women's volleyball programs will introduce a new Taraflex® court for the 2026-27 seasons in LionTree Arena. The Tritons' new playing surface made its debut for the women's volleyball home opener on Sept. 25 against Cal State Fullerton.
The same world-class playing surface used at the Olympics and the NCAA Division I Women's Volleyball Championship is now home to the Tritons. Featuring a bold ocean-inspired design, the new court reflects UC San Diego's commitment to building an elite volleyball program and one of the premier collegiate volleyball environments on the West Coast.
 FUTURE WCC FOES 
Preparing for the department's 2027 transition to the West Coast Conference, Coach McLachlin stacked the preseason with a plethora of matches against the Tritons' future conference opponents. UC San Diego has four WCC matchups on the schedule this season, including Saint Mary's (W, 3-1), Gonzaga (W, 3-1), Loyola Marymount (L, 3-1) and Pacific (W, 3-0). The Tritons finished 3-1 against their future conference foes.
 McCLUSKEY NAMED OFFENSIVE PLAYER OF THE WEEK (OCT. 26) 
Junior opposite Molly McCluskey led the Big West with 5.28 points per set—totaling 47.5 points as the Tritons split a weekend series with UC Irvine. McCluskey averaged 4.67 kills on a .267 hitting percentage, adding 2.78 digs per set with back-to-back double-doubles. She also added seven blocks and two service aces in nine sets. On Friday, McCluskey tallied 18 kills, 14 digs and four blocks for 21.0 points in a five-set loss to the Anteaters. On Saturday, she recorded a season-best 24 kills and 26.5 points, adding 11 digs and three blocks in a four-set road victory at Irvine. She currently ranks second in the Big West in total points and total kills.
 RIVERA EARNS SECOND BIG WEST WEEKLY HONOR (OCT. 12) 
True freshman Gia Rivera earned her second Big West Rookie of the Week nod of the season after leading the Tritons offensively with 4.57 points and 4.43 kills per set. Rivera recorded a team-best 31 kills on 60 swings with just six errors for a .417 hitting percentage. She also added six digs and one block assist, finishing with 32.0 points. On Friday, Rivera tallied a team-high 18 kills with a .412 hitting percentage, adding four digs and one block against Sacramento State. She led the offense once again on Saturday, recording 13 kills on 26 swings with just two errors for a career-best .423 hitting percentage in a three-set sweep of Utah Valley.
 McNEES NAMED BIG WEST OFFENSIVE PLAYER OF THE WEEK (OCT. 5) 
 Ireland McNees was dominant for the Tritons in a 2-0 week, averaging 5.00 points and 4.56 kills with a .405 hitting percentage to earn her first Big West weekly honor. The senior outside hitter tallied 41 total kills and 45.0 points to lead the team, adding two aces and four blocks. She also averaged 1.33 digs over nine sets. In a 3-1 win at California Baptist, McNees recorded 19 kills on 35 swings with zero errors for a .543 hitting percentage. She registered a career-best 22 kills and 25.5 points to lead the Tritons in a five-set victory at UC Riverside.
 RIVERA NAMED BIG WEST ROOKIE OF THE WEEK (SEPT. 14) 
 Gia Rivera was named Big West Rookie of the Week after a strong performance at the Borderland Classic. The freshman outside hitter averaged 3.70 points per set and finished second on the team with 37 total points over three matches. Rivera averaged 3.50 kills with a .237 hitting percentage, adding nine total digs and four blocks over 10 sets.
On Friday at New Mexico State, Rivera recorded career highs with 20 kills and 22.0 points, adding three digs and four blocks with a .279 hitting percentage. She followed with 13 kills and five digs at UTEP on Saturday, recording her fourth consecutive double-figure kills total.
 McCLUSKEY EARNS SECOND UCU ATHLETE OF THE WEEK NOD (SEPT. 14) 
 Molly McCluskey led the Tritons at the Borderland Classic, averaging 4.29 points, 3.83 kills and 2.58 digs in 12 sets. The junior opposite hit at a .279 clip, totaling 46 kills and adding nine blocks and one service ace for a team-best 51.5 points. McCluskey recorded two double-doubles over the weekend, bringing her total to six in nine matches this season. On Friday at New Mexico State she tallied 22 kills, 13 digs, six blocks and 25 points, hitting .357. Against UTEP, she collected 14 kills and six digs, before wrapping up the weekend against Pacific with 10 kills and 12 digs.
 McCLUSKEY NAMED UCU ATHLETE OF THE WEEK (AUG. 31) 
 Molly McCluskey was a standout on opening weekend, leading UC San Diego to a 2-1 finish at the Gael Bear Classic. The junior opposite averaged 4.33 points, 3.33 kills and 2.42 digs across 12 sets for the Tritons, recording two double-doubles. She also tallied a conference-best seven service aces and added nine blocks to finish the weekend with 52 points. McCluskey began the weekend with 12 kills and 12 digs in the season opener against Saint Mary's, adding five aces and four blocks for 19.5 points. She followed with another double-double against Cal, totaling 13 kills and 13 digs and finished the weekend with 15 kills and a .333 hitting percentage against Gonzaga.
 MOLLY McCLUSKEY NAMED TO PRESEASON TEAM 
Junior opposite Molly McCluskey was selected as a member of the 2026 Big West Preseason Coaches' Team after earning All-Big West Honorable Mention last season. In 2025, McCluskey finished first in the Big West in total points (449.0) and total kills (392) for the regular season. She also ranked fourth in total attacks (1,033) and fifth in kills per set (3.41). The Costa Mesa native led the Tritons in points, kills and service aces (27), finishing second in blocks (55.0) and third in digs (244).
 TRITON RETURNERS 
UC San Diego returns three starters from a season ago, including senior Ireland McNees (outside hitter) and juniors Paulina Baillie (libero) and Molly McCluskey (opposite). The Tritons will also benefit from the experience of Maija Nepszy (setter), Madison Johnson (middle) and Lucia Barroso (middle) who each played significant roles for UC San Diego last season. The senior class includes Marleena Catalan , Katelyn Hernandez and Ireland McNees .
 FRESH FACES 
UC San Diego women's volleyball will add 10 newcomers to its roster for the 2026 season. The Tritons will welcome five first-year scholar-athletes, including Soraya Dennis (Laguna Beach, Calif.), Kylie Parker (Burbank, Calif.), Gia Rivera (Redwood City, Calif.), Hayden Shanafelt (San Clemente, Calif.) and Ahnika Smith (Manhattan Beach, Calif.). 
Transfers Yasemin Elmas (Istanbul, Turkey), Dillyn Griffin (Foothill Ranch, Calif.), Jaedyn Houston (Newport Beach, Calif.), Brynne McGhie (Kansas City, Mo.) and Kaliya Ndiaye (Aliso Viejo, Calif.) join UC San Diego after competing for Seattle U, Pitt, Long Beach State, Pepperdine and Syracuse, respectively.
 ROAD WARRIORS 
UC San Diego will play its entire non-conference slate on the road, traveling for 11 matches spread across four tournaments before Big West play begins at home Sept. 25. The Tritons will begin in the Bay Area with the Gael Bear Classic, hosted by Saint Mary's and Cal (Aug. 28-30). UC San Diego will then travel to Coach McLachlin's hometown for the Outrigger Invitational hosted at former Big West foe Hawai'i (Sept. 3-6). The Borderland Classic will be hosted by New Mexico State and UTEP (Sept. 11-13) and the non-conference schedule will wrap up in Las Vegas with The Rebel Challenge hosted at UNLV (Sept. 19-20).
 TRITONS PICKED TO FINISH EIGHTH 
In their final year as a member of the Big West, the Tritons were picked to finish eighth in the Big West Preseason Coaches' Poll with 60 points. Cal Poly led the group with 121 points and 11 of the 12 first-place votes in the Big West's newly formatted 12-team conference. 
Long Beach State ranked second with 109 points and UC Santa Barbara rounded out the top three with 99 points. Big West newcomers Utah Valley (84 points) and Sacramento State (80) were picked to finish fourth and fifth respectively, with UVU receiving the remaining first-place vote. CSUN and UC Irvine tied for sixth with 64 points each, followed by the Tritons, newcomer California Baptist (35), UC Riverside (34), Cal State Fullerton (24) and Cal State Bakersfield (18).
 McLACHLIN NAMED EIGHTH HEAD COACH IN PROGRAM HISTORY 
On December 23, 2025, UC San Diego Director of Athletics Andy Fee named Spencer McLachlin the new women's volleyball head coach. McLachlin becomes the eighth head coach in program history. 
McLachlin recently completed his third season as an associate head coach for the USC women's volleyball program. In 2025, he helped lead the Women of Troy to 25 wins, a fourth-place finish in the ultra-competitive Big Ten, and their fourth-consecutive NCAA second round appearance. 
Previously, McLachlin served as the associate head coach at Indiana (2022) and was an assistant coach for the UCLA men's volleyball program for four years (2018-2021). He has also had experience coaching at the international level with the U.S. men's national team where he was on staffs for squads which competed in the Pan American Cup and NORCECA Champions cup. Additionally, McLachlin had stints as an assistant coach at California (2016-2017) and Hawai'i men's volleyball (2015), earning him recognition on the American Volleyball Coaches Association (AVCA) Thirty Under 30 list in 2017. 
McLachlin competed as a student-athlete at Stanford (2008-11) as an outside hitter, where he won a national championship with the Cardinal in 2010. He graduated from Stanford with a degree in political science in 2011 and completed a Master of Education in 2012 while serving as a club coach for the Bay-to-Bay Volleyball Club.
As a professional athlete, McLachlin was an outside hitter for Mas NIKI Aiginio in Greece for three years from 2012 to 2014. McLachlin and his wife Diane have three children: daughters Leila and Malia, and a son, Koa.
 NEW STAFF FOR TRITONS 
McLachlin completed his coaching staff for the 2026 season with the addition of associate head coach Jimmy Lundgren , assistant coaches Casey Schoenlein and Kat Chen and technical coordinator Frank Pham . Lundgren joins the Tritons after stints at California Baptist (2025) and the University of San Diego (2018-2024). Schoenlein also comes to La Jolla from USD, spending three seasons with the Toreros (2023-2025). Chen served on the staff at UC Santa Barbara (2024-2026) and was also an assistant coach and manager for the Australian Senior Women's National Team (2023-24), bringing a wealth of international knowledge to the Tritons' staff. Pham is a 2026 graduate of Cal Poly, having served as technical coordinator for the Big West champions (2022-2026) throughout his undergrad and also serves as assistant performance analyst for the U.S. Men's National Team. 
 UC SAN DIEGO HEADED TO THE WCC 
On Sept. 3, 2025, UC San Diego accepted a formal invitation to join the West Coast Conference (WCC) beginning July 1, 2027. UC San Diego will compete in 14 of the West Coast Conference's 16 sponsored sports, including men's and women's basketball, men's and women's soccer, women's volleyball, men's and women's cross country, men's water polo, baseball, softball, men's and women's tennis, men's golf and women's rowing. The university remains committed to finding a conference affiliation for its sports that will not compete in the West Coast Conference.
Beginning in 2027-28, the WCC membership will consist of: University of California San Diego, Loyola Marymount University, University of the Pacific, Pepperdine University, University of Portland, Saint Mary's College, University of San Diego, University of San Francisco, Santa Clara University, and Seattle University. UC San Diego will become the first public institution in the West Coast Conference since the departure of the University of Nevada-Reno in 1979.
 ANDY FEE NAMED ATHLETIC DIRECTOR AT UC SAN DIEGO  
On Sept. 10, 2025, UC San Diego Chancellor Pradeep K. Khosla announced the hiring of college sports veteran Andy Fee as the Tritons' new Director of Athletics. Fee will become just the fourth Director of Athletics at UC San Diego since 1966. Fee joins the Tritons after spending the 2024-25 season as Deputy AD at Seattle University. Prior to Seattle U, Fee spent two years at Washington as Deputy AD and Chief of Staff. 
Before relocating to Seattle, Fee spent five years as Director of Athletics at Long Beach State from 2017 to 2022. During this time, Long Beach State's athletic programs found great success as the school advanced to the postseason in 18 of its 19 sports programs in his five-year tenure. The Beach won a pair of national championships in men's volleyball and claimed The Big West Commissioner's Cup three times. 
No stranger to conference transition, Fee will help guide the Tritons into the West Coast Conference in 2027-28. He also helped guide Washington into the Big Ten and Seattle U into the WCC in July.
 WHY THE TRITONS? 
The Triton is described as the offspring of Poseidon and Amphitrite, a demigod of the sea with a lower part of the body like that of a fish. It is known as a mighty and fierce sea warrior. Given UC San Diego's close proximity to the Pacific Ocean and its connections with the world-famous Scripps Institution of Oceanography, the Triton became our mascot in 1964.
 UC SAN DIEGO ON THE WORLDWIDE LEADER 
Most UC San Diego home men's and women's basketball games, men's and women's soccer matches, men's and women's volleyball matches, baseball and softball games are broadcast live on ESPN+. For more information on where to watch UC San Diego women's volleyball, visit UCSDTritons.com/live.
 GAME DAY GOES DIGITAL 
Triton fans now have a whole new way to access game day information, as game programs have gone digital! Fans can visit UCSDTritons.com from their smart phone or scan the QR code at the entrance to LionTree Arena for everything they need to know about each home game, including updated rosters, schedules, and stats for each team, as well as links to watch on ESPN+.
 COVERING THE TRITONS 
Media members wishing to cover a UC San Diego game in-person at LionTree Arena must notify a member of the Athletics Communication staff no later than 24 hours prior to the game. Following the conclusion of each home game, a video highlight melt and video postgame interviews will be made available for media members to download.
 GET SOCIAL WITH UC SAN DIEGO WOMEN'S VOLLEYBALL 
Keep up with the Tritons all season long on social media through X and Instagram. The team's handle is @ucsdwvb.
 FOR THE YOUNGER CROWD 
Got some young Triton fans in your family? If they are eighth grade or under, check out the Junior Triton Club. Membership includes a free t-shirt, admission to over 100 UC San Diego home athletic events, and much more!

 About UC San Diego Athletics 
 After two decades as one of the most successful programs in NCAA Division II, the UC San Diego intercollegiate athletics program began a new era in 2020 as a member of The Big West in NCAA Division I. The 23-sport Tritons earned 30 team and nearly 150 individual national championships during its time in Divisions II and III and helped guide 1,400 scholar-athletes to All-America honors. A total of 84 Tritons have earned Academic All-America honors, while 38 have earned prestigious NCAA Post Graduate Scholarships. UC San Diego scholar-athletes exemplify the academic ideals of one of the world's preeminent institutions, graduating at an average rate of 91 percent, one of the highest rates among institutions at all divisions.
